author: reek
body: The record keeps its shape because callers use it, but the fields now mean what the producer actually puts in them: `scan-code` and `char-code` are both the poll-key value (a CCE code point, or a named key), and `shift-state` is `poll-mods` with the validity bit set.

author: reek
body: Insert has no poll-key value: `sk-high` maps no scancode to it, so this is honestly False rather than a comparison that cannot fire. Wiring Insert means giving it a named key in KeyInput first.

author: reek
body: A Ctrl chord is the letter plus the ctrl bit, which is what poll-key answers. These compared `char-code` against ASCII control codes -- Ctrl+C as 3, Ctrl+S as 19 -- and poll-key has never produced one, so not a single chord below has ever fired. `key-upper` folds the case so the chord works whether or not shift or caps is in play.
